sections.label: Singapore warming and hot days
sections.summary: Meteorological Service reports 2013-2022 was Singapore's warmest decade, with the urban environment a significant factor, and very hot days increasing.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The latest Meteorological Service reports says that the 10-year period, from 2013 to 2022, was Singapore's warmest on record with the man-made urban environment as a significant contributing factor.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The number of very hot days where daily maximum mean temperature exceeds 35°C has also increased over the last few decades and according to the third National Climate Change study, will continue to increase depending on how fast Singapore and the world decarbonises.

sections.label: Sea level protection spending
sections.summary: In 2019 the Government announced it may spend $100 billion or more to protect the island from rising sea levels.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2019, the Government announced that it may spend $100 billion or more to protect the island from rising sea levels.

sections.label: Heat reflective paint pilot
sections.summary: A pilot study coated 130 Tampines HDB blocks with heat reflective paint, and subsidies are hoped for to roll it out to rental flat blocks.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For instance, the pilot study of the 130 Tampines HDB blocks coated with heat reflective paint is a good example of a project that takes a preventive approach to increasing temperatures.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given that this type of paint costs more, we hope that there can be subsidies given to roll this out to rental flat blocks if the results are promising.

sections.label: Green Building Masterplan targets
sections.summary: The Singapore Green Building Masterplan sets a 2030 target of 80% of buildings Green Mark-certified and an 80% energy efficiency improvement from a 2005 baseline.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the Singapore Green Building Masterplan has set a 2030 target for 80% of buildings to be Green Mark-certified – 80% of new developments to be super low energy and an 80% energy efficiency improvement from a 2005 baseline.

sections.label: Regulation to tackle heat
sections.summary: Regulation plays an important role in tackling heat, including possible legislation for MCST solar panels, climate impact assessments and free tap water at F&B establishments.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Third, and finally, I would like to make the point that regulation plays an important role in tackling our problems with heat in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These can be new things that we have not done yet, like considering the development of legislation that makes easier for condominium Management Corporations Strata Title (MCSTs) to install solar panels, which shade buildings and reduce demand for fossil fuel powered electricity.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We can explore the need for climate change impact assessments for new infrastructure and potentially require food and beverage (F&B) establishments to serve hydrating and healthy tap water for free.

sections.label: Water coolers at MRT stations
sections.summary: The Land Transport Authority could fit all MRT stations with water coolers, given Singaporeans are the world's biggest per capita spenders on bottled water.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Land Transport Authority could also fit all Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) stations with water coolers in a quick and meaningful intervention – given that people in Singapore are the biggest spenders on bottled water in the world on a per capita basis, according to a United Nations (UN) think tank report in 2023; and this is even though our tap water is highly drinkable and well regulated.

sections.label: National heat resilience strategy
sections.summary: The Government adopts a science-based heat resilience strategy with three prongs: national cooling, community resilience and scientific understanding.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The Government adopts a science-based and proactive heat resilience strategy, which has three prongs: first, implementing national-level cooling strategies to benefit all segments of our society, including the vulnerable; second, strengthening the community's resilience, especially among more vulnerable population segments; and, third, deepening our scientific understanding of the impact of rising temperatures.

sections.label: Heat Stress Advisory launch
sections.summary: The Heat Stress Advisory was launched in July last year to guide the public on minimising heat stress risk.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Second, we have taken steps to empower the community to cope with a warming world.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We launched the Heat Stress Advisory in July last year, to guide the public on ways to minimise the risk of heat stress.

sections.label: Rest breaks for workers
sections.summary: Employers must provide a minimum 10-minute hourly rest break under shade for workers doing heavy physical activities when WBGT is 32 or higher.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Of note, employers are required to provide a minimum rest break of 10 minutes hourly under shade, for workers carrying out heavy physical activities when the WBGT is 32 or higher.

sections.label: Cooling Singapore 2.0 project
sections.summary: The Cooling Singapore 2.0 project is developing a digital model to simulate Singapore's urban climate and assess cooling strategies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: For example, the Cooling Singapore 2.0 project is developing a digital model, to simulate Singapore's urban climate and assess the effectiveness of various cooling strategies.

sections.label: Climate Impact Science Research Programme
sections.summary: The Climate Impact Science Research Programme will examine rising temperatures' effects on health and second-order effects, with NUS centre as a network node.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Through the Climate Impact Science Research Programme, we will examine the effects of rising temperatures on our physical and mental health as well as second-order effects, such as increased mosquito population.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The Heat Resilience and Performance Centre at NUS will be the Southeast Asia node of the Global Heat Health Information Network, an initiative by the World Health Organization and World Meteorological Organization.

sections.label: Time-resilient Parliament remark
sections.summary: Beyond a heat-resilient Singapore, the speaker says there is a time-resilient Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Beyond a heat-resilient Singapore, I think we do have a time-resilient Parliament.
